name: Biokinetics 2
editorial_article: "Biokinetics 2" is a seminal track from the 1996 album *Biokinetics* by the German duo Porter Ricks. Released on the legendary Chain Reaction label—a subsidiary of Basic Channel—the track is a cornerstone of the dub techno movement that defined the mid-90s Berlin electronic scene. Composed by Andy Mellwig and Thomas Köner, the piece exemplifies the "Chain Reaction sound": a fusion of skeletal, driving techno percussion with deep, reverberated soundscapes that evoke industrial maritime decay. \n\nMusically, "Biokinetics 2" is characterized by its hypnotic, rhythmic cycles, where cold, mechanical beats are submerged under layers of shimmering, aqueous dub echoes. The production is deliberately sparse yet atmospheric, focusing on texture and space rather than melodic development. It serves as a bridge between ambient music and dub techno, showcasing the unique ability of Porter Ricks to create immersive, almost tactile sound environments. The track remains highly regarded for its dark, brooding aesthetic and its influence on subsequent generations of producers exploring the intersection of minimalism and dub. It was famously reissued in 2012 by Type Records, further cementing its status as a timeless piece of electronic music history. Its resonance lies in its ability to balance intense mechanical precision with a deep, haunting sense of isolation. The track captures the essence of the Chain Reaction label’s philosophy, providing an experience that is at once physically demanding and psychologically deep. Through the deft use of delay and sonic layering, Mellwig and Köner created an aquatic sound world that still feels forward-thinking decades later.
